/> Even paler. <break time="0.8s" /> He wandered from room to room. <break time="0.8s" /> Without purpose. <break time="0.8s" /> And sometimes he sat for hours. <break time="0.8s" /> Staring into empty space. <break time="0.8s" /> As if listening to some imaginary sound. <break time="0.8s" /> On the seventh or eighth night. <break time="0.8s" /> After we had placed her in the vault. <break time="0.8s" /> I could not sleep. <break time="0.8s" /> And an unknown fear. <break time="0.8s" /> Crept into my heart. <break time="0.8s" /> Soon Usher knocked gently at my door. <break time="0.8s" /> And entered with a lamp. <break time="0.8s" /> And in his eyes there was a kind of wild, held back excitement. <break time="0.8s" /> And you have not seen it. <break time="0.8s" /> He said. <break time="0.8s" /> And he threw open a window. <break time="0.8s" /> To the storm. <break time="0.8s" /> Which was wild yet strangely beautiful. <break time="0.8s" /> The heavy clouds were flying. <break time="0.8s" /> In all directions. <break time="0.8s" /> And a strange, glowing mist. <break time="0.8s" /> Hung around the house. <break time="0.8s" /> Though there was neither moon nor lightning. <break time="0.8s" /> Closing the window. <break time="0.8s" /> I began to read aloud. <break time="0.8s" /> An old romance called Mad Trist. <break time="0.8s" /> By Sir Launcelot Canning. <break time="0.8s" /> Hoping that it would calm my friend. <break time="0.8s" /> When I read. <break time="0.8s" /> How the hero Ethelred broke down a wooden door. <break time="0.8s" /> There came from a distant part of the house. <break time="0.8s" /> A cracking and ripping sound. <break time="0.8s" /> Then the story told of a dragons terrible shriek. <break time="0.8s" /> And at that very moment. <break time="0.8s" /> I heard a long, harsh, screaming sound. <break time="0.8s" /> From somewhere far away.
